title: The generated Cora project
text: This is the actual Vivado twenty-twenty-five-point-one project generated for the Cora Z seven dash ten. The system block design is open in the real Vivado G U I, so the cells, interfaces, clocks, resets, and address-connected peripherals shown here are the implementation source, not a presentation diagram.
evidence: Vivado opens the generated XPR and system.bd, and every named demonstration cell exists.

title: Host memory and streaming DMA
text: The highlighted A X I D M A block is the software-facing entrance and exit for acoustic samples. Its memory-to-stream channel feeds the acoustic router, while stream-to-memory returns each completed frame. Linux therefore keeps one stable device interface even when the processing chain in programmable logic changes.
evidence: Vivado resolves and highlights axi_dma_dsp and the data interconnect in the open block design.

title: Known-good AXIS loopback
text: The acoustic router is the bring-up anchor. In loopback mode it returns the D M A stream directly while preserving valid, ready, and last signaling. That gives new hardware a known-good test before any algorithm core is enabled, and software selects the path without rebuilding the block design.
evidence: The real axis_acomms_router_0 cell is selected and highlighted.

title: Installed accelerator chain
text: The alternate route passes through the forward F F T, the spectral-filter example, and the inverse F F T before returning to the router. This chain demonstrates the insertion contract with a working accelerator while keeping the direct loopback beside it for diagnosis.
evidence: Vivado highlights the three installed accelerator cells in sequence on the actual canvas.

title: Control, clocks, and reset
text: A X I Lite control reaches the router and spectral filter through the control interconnect. The streaming path uses the one-hundred-megahertz fabric clock and its matching reset network. A custom core should share this domain, or add explicit clock conversion when its interface requires another rate.
evidence: The highlighted control and reset cells exist and connect to the two controlled streaming blocks.

title: Where custom IP connects
text: To insert your own processing, keep the router and replace the example chain between its accelerator output and accelerator return interfaces. Match the thirty-two-bit A X I stream width, propagate backpressure and T last, then assign any new A X I Lite registers a non-overlapping address before validating the design.
evidence: The highlighted router and replaceable example chain identify the concrete insertion region.

title: Return to the complete design
text: Returning to the full canvas shows why this structure is reusable: software and D M A remain fixed, loopback remains available, and only the accelerator segment changes. The checked-in Tcl script regenerates this project, while the exported X S A carries the result into the common PetaLinux build.
evidence: The complete live system block design is visible again in Vivado.
